text:
Liam Park: Heads-up — prepping Northlight QBR cost slide. Need token burn (30/60/90), embed pilot delta, and any procurement/credit risks. @Zoe can you grab spend windows and note any anomalous jobs?

Zoe Patel: On it. Ill pull raw token totals and isolate Dedicated pilot embed traffic. Want blended or separate lines?

Liam Park: Separate lines please (hosted vs dedicated) + a combined forecast. Procurement flagged a possible invoice hold if month-over-month spend >20%. Call that out.

Ethan Kim: Noted two things: 1) They enabled a bulk export in the middle of the month that doubled seq length for some runs; 2) Their volume discount tier triggers at 500M tokens/month — theyre close. Could be leverage in renewal.

Zoe Patel: Quick numbers draft:
```
30d total: 65,400,000 tokens
60d total: 120,300,000 tokens
90d total: 188,900,000 tokens
Dedicated-embed pilot (last 30d): 7.2M tokens
Current run-rate: ~2.05M tokens/day
Forecast baseline (90d): 195-230M tokens
```

Liam Park: Good. Can you produce three scenarios (conservative/likely/aggressive) and show impact on hitting the 500M tier? Also estimate monthly cost delta and a suggested annualized spend band for renewal pricing.

Zoe Patel: Will do. Assumptions: conservative = no embed conversion improvement; likely = 20% of text queries convert to embed when pilot goes prod; aggressive = 45% conversion + onboarding completes. Ill calc both token and embed-unit cost impacts.

Ethan Kim: Risk note: the bulk export caused one-day 90% token spike on 1777920000. Recommend temporary alert: single-day tokens > 3x daily median -> automatic review + throttle. Also recommend a short-term credit or invoice buffer if spike was platform-driven.

Liam Park: Procurement hold risk is elevated if forecast variance > 20%. Include an exec bullet proposing a small contingency credit (range: $5k-$20k) to smooth the renewal conversation.

cs-bot: QBR template reminder: use the "cost-summary" and "procurement-risk" sections. Link: https://redwood.company/qbr-templates

Zoe Patel: Draft slide plan: 1) snapshot + anomalies, 2) scenarios vs discount tiers, 3) mitigations + asks for procurement. Ill add a sensitivity chart.

Liam Park: Enablement asks: quick enablement on embedding batching, a one-hour walk-through of quota guards, and an itemized suggested credit. Who can run these? @Ethan?

Ethan Kim: I can run batching + quota guard walkthrough. Will prepare a 30-min demo focused on seq-length best practices and batching knobs.

Zoe Patel: Uploaded preliminary numbers: https://drive.redwood/northlight/qbr-numbers — pulled raw logs and highlighted spikes.

Liam Park: Action items:
- Zoe: finalize scenarios + sensitivity chart by Mon 9am PT (1778086800)
- Ethan: prep demo + propose time by Mon EOD
- Liam: draft exec ask (credit range + negotiation talking points) by Tue noon

Zoe Patel: Quick callout: if they hit the 500M tier, blended unit cost drops ~11% — include as a renewal leverage point.

Ethan Kim: Ran a small throttle test in staging for bulk exports: CPU up 3%, latency +12ms, embed batch token-cost -18% at batching=256. Will paste perf snippet in drive.

Liam Park: Perfect. Also surface any onboarding blockers that delay reaching the aggressive scenario — e.g., SSO or API keys misconfig. Zoe, add a short line on onboarding completion % and impact.

Zoe Patel: Onboarding status: 62% seats active (SSO partial), estimated full activation in ~6 weeks if SSO completes. Ill quantify token uplift for 6/12 week horizons.

Liam Park: Great. Final ask: call out three short-term mitigations in the exec summary: 1) temporary throttle/alert on export spikes, 2) batching knobs for embeds, 3) contingency credit range to avoid procurement hold.

Zoe Patel: Putting slides together now. Will tag Ethan for numbers on the batching slide.

Ethan Kim: I'll record a 10-min clip demonstrating quota guard config and upload it.

Liam Park: Thanks all. Drop anything else here; Ill combine into the QBR folder and ping legal if we escalate credit approval. :thumbsup:
